title: [Chapitre] VIII. Analysis situs (quatrième mouture) : notes manuscrites (26/06-04/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the surrounding pages): Grothendieck is building a purely combinatorial 'analysis situs' of dimension 1. There is a stratified model M whose strata are points P_x and open segments S_ab (a<b) of a finite ordered set. A polygone Φ is a finite set of such strata, a union of cells. Figures are the closed ones and préfigures the not-necessarily-closed ones. Relations between strata include |Z|⊂|X| (incidence/inclusion of underlying sets), ≤ and its strict form, and ≤° (the 'interior' version).

The previous page proves that every polygone decomposes uniquely as a disjoint union Φ_D of its connected components. More precisely, D ↦ Φ_D = ⋃_{Φ∈D} Φ is a bijection from finite strictly separated families of connected polygones (Dr*_{!<}(Polygconn(M))) to Polyg(M).

This page first completes statement 4):
- Φ_D is closed iff each component Φ∈D is closed.
- Φ_D is open iff each component is open.

It then remarks on method. So far, in describing polygones and figures, only the relation |·| and the explicit order relations ≤, < have been used, not the other relations. Now that he passes to supports, this will no longer suffice.

It then sets up a programme to compute explicitly supp°Φ, the (open) support of an arbitrary polygone, i.e. the set of strata Z of M lying in it:
- (1°) Additivity: if Φ has connected components Φ_i, then supp°Φ = ⊔_i supp°Φ_i (disjoint union).
- (2°) Computation for Φ connected, in three steps. The next page gives these: (a) the irreducible cases, namely a point, a closed segment, and a half-open segment; (b) the general case via a chain T and its boundary {or T, ex T}.

The margin note seems to be a reminder that the last two assertions belong to the overall strategy, that orientation still has to be treated, and that something called Δ is missing.

The problem served is a finite, combinatorial ('tame') model of the topology of the line and of 1-dimensional polygonal sets, with closure, interior, connectedness and support all computed by order-theoretic formulas.
errors: No mathematical error. The closed/open criterion for disjoint unions of separated components and the additivity of supports are both correct, given that components are mutually separated: their closures are disjoint, so local properties are checked componentwise.

ideas.what: A polygone is open (resp. closed) iff each of its connected components is open (resp. closed).
ideas.modern_name: Topology of finite unions of cells / clopen decomposition into separated components

ideas.what: Additivity of the support over connected components: supp°Φ = ⊔ supp°Φ_i.
ideas.modern_name: Additivity of cell-complex supports / finite stratified set calculus

ideas.what: Programme of a purely combinatorial tame topology of dimension 1 via ordered models of points and segments.
ideas.modern_name: Tame topology / o-minimal-style cell decomposition; finite T0 spaces / face posets
ideas.usually_credited_to: van den Dries, Pillay–Steinhorn, Knight (o-minimality); Grothendieck's call in Esquisse d'un programme
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984), section on 'topologie modérée' (programme only, no such combinatorics)

deep.surprise_reason: A bookkeeping page in a long combinatorial development. It completes an elementary open/closed criterion and announces the routine additivity of supports. The broader 1986 Analysis situs project is itself little-known, but nothing on this page is a new result or connection.
transcription_corrections: 'rapp°' should read 'supp°' (support), consistent with the next page; likewise 'rapports' should be 'supports' ('maintenant que je passe aux supports'; 'détermination explicite des supports d'un polygone quelconque').
The fraction '\frac{\mathfrak{L}}{D}' is the subscripted Φ_D (letter Φ, as on the previous page), not a quotient; '\mathfrak{L}' throughout should be Φ.
'maintenant que je pense aux' is more likely 'maintenant que je passe aux'.
'Cela se fait en plusieurs étapes' - 'une polygone' should be 'un polygone'.
